html:
The Zoró, who call themselves Pangyjej, are an Indigenous people of northwestern Mato Grosso, Brazil, near the border with Rondônia.

They speak a Mondé language of the Tupi family, close to those of the Paiter Suruí, the Gavião Ikolen and the Cinta Larga, with whom they often fought. Government agents contacted them in 1977 as roads and settlers reached the region, and disease soon cut their numbers. Today they live in the Zoró Indigenous Territory.
